panicle, often up to 60 cm (24 in) long

appearance.value: pink or dull-purple tinge when ripe, turning golden brown with the foliage in fall
appearance.quote: sometimes take on a pink or dull-purple tinge

architecture.value: lowland types look bunchgrass-like; upland types are more sod-forming
architecture.quote: the lowland cultivars may appear to have a bunchgrass habit, while the upland types tend to be more sod-forming
Its flowers have a well-developed panicle

architecture.value: deep fibrous roots and short rhizomes

phenology.when: growth begins in late spring and most growth is late spring through early fall; dormant in colder months
phenology.quote: most of its growth occurs from late spring through early fall

propagation.fact: dormant and unproductive during colder months
propagation.quote: it becomes dormant and unproductive during colder months

uses_real.note: Drought-resistant ornamental in average to wet soils, full sun to part shade.
uses_real.quote: grown as a drought-resistant ornamental grass

uses_real.note: Cellulosic ethanol, biogas, pellets and direct combustion.

uses_real.quote: as ground cover for soil conservation, and to control erosion
for forages and grazing, as game cover

life_form.quote: is a perennial warm season bunchgrass

description.value: Hardy, deep-rooted perennial warm-season bunchgrass up to 2.7 m tall with long leaves and large open panicles.
description.quote: Switchgrass is a hardy, deep-rooted, perennial rhizomatous grass

native_range.value: North America, from 55 N in Canada south into the United States and Mexico
native_range.quote: native to North America, where it occurs naturally from 55°N latitude in Canada southwards into the United States and Mexico

environment.value: Dominant species of the central North American tallgrass prairie, also remnant prairies, pastures and roadsides.
environment.quote: one of the dominant species of the central North American tallgrass prairie

flowers.quote: Its flowers have a well-developed panicle

fruit.description: Seeds 3-6 mm long, pink or dull-purple when ripe, golden brown in fall.
